system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status note:** No written authority from Amelia Frost has been received on any fallback position. All recommendations below therefore hold the playbook starting positions. The Seller's "fair and balanced" framing and the Disclosure Letter's reservation at [11] do not bind us; several Seller summary statements are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, which is flagged where relevant.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** 20% is our conditional fallback only, and no Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft exists.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three limbs.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure would absorb a material tranche of recoverable loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a default that every limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims expressly.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter 24 months and strike the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval (none given), and the catch-all language is a hidden override of the separate regimes (see N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum 6 years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Collapsing title/capacity into a 20% / 18-month regime removes core protection for the thing we are actually buying; "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Insert an express, non-waivable fraud carve-out; non-negotiable.** The Seller's wording would purport to limit liability for the Seller's own fraud, which is unacceptable and in any event of doubtful enforceability.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2]).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject [1.1]–[1.2]; require disclosures to be specific and fairly made with sufficient detail.** Whole-room disclosure would gut the warranties by deeming every undiscovered issue disclosed.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: blanket exclusion deleted; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, and never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. (Playbook also requires any Seller knowledge qualifiers to reference named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry.)
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3 entirely.** "Discoverable" plus adviser knowledge is a constructive-knowledge bar that compounds the N-006 problem and would make the warranty package largely illusory.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL [2] confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: a Completion condition requiring effective consent AND evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; stronger than reasonable endeavours.
- Recommendation: **Reject; hard CP with evidence of satisfied conditions.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) and the Seller's own letter admits the consent and conditions are outstanding – "addressed" in the update is not accurate.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: release to follow Completion (cl 2/7). DL [3] confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release; require payout, direct repayment and releases at Completion.** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot complete with AUD 3.2m secured debt and change-of-control exposure (cl 8.1) left live.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 AUD 420,000 is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in funds flow. DL [5] confirms the amounts are absent from the funds flow and is silent on on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs as a specific line item in the funds flow or expressly Seller-funded.
- Recommendation: **Require express line item (bonus + on-costs) or Seller-funded mechanism; reject silence.** "A matter for the Seller" with no contractual mechanism leaves the Company (i.e. us post-Completion) bearing the cost.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL [4]: transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; AUD 180,000 shown open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering title/ownership of SOW3 materials, third-party claims and remediation costs, while preserving the cure (pay outstanding fee and obtain confirmatory assignment). Treat AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.
- Recommendation: **Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it and require pre-Completion cure or escrow.** The exposure is loss of IP ownership, not just a AUD 180,000 payment, and the figure itself is unverified.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL [6]: ~1,240 records, access and notification status unknown, investigation preliminary, no loss stated.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, ongoing updates to Completion, and a specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident costs. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum either way.
- Recommendation: **Require preservation/investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity; reject "not expected to be material" as a contractual conclusion.** The Seller's own letter says the facts are not yet established, so neither side can characterise it as immaterial or material.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. DL [8]: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008/DD-011); silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: assessment of timing, termination rights and accrual status; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label; request the renewal terms and reserve position pending assessment.** The Seller's disclosure expressly does not support its own summary characterisation.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13), limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5), and Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Title/Tax/IP/payment obligations/covenants and specific indemnities each in their own expressly separate regime; no general-regime override.
- Recommendation: **Strike all catch-all language and insert an express carve-out clause listing the separate regimes.** Each of the Seller's three formulations is a hidden override that would silently pull Title, Tax, IP and specific indemnities under the 20% / 18-month cap.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title to 100% evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL [10] admits this is merely the source relied on, not independent verification.
- Buyer wants: independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence (ASIC searches, PPSR, board/shareholder authorisations, no-encumbrance confirmations, Riverlark release tie-in).
- Recommendation: **Treat DD-012 as insufficient; obtain independent verification before signing.** A Seller-supplied internal register is not proof of title, and the Seller's own letter concedes the point.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: terms remain OPEN; separate Tax and IP regimes to be negotiated; no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution assumed.
- Recommendation: **Reject "settled"; record Tax/IP as open and outside the general regime.** The Seller is attempting to close these by assertion, and subsuming them in the general cap conflicts with N-004 and N-014.

---

## Summary
No Seller position is acceptable as drafted. The most significant points for the response letter are: the absence of any fraud carve-out (N-005), the collapse of Title/Tax/IP into the general regime (N-004/N-014/N-016), the data-room and "discoverable" knowledge bars (N-006/N-007), and the three deal-mechanics items the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts – Bluefen (N-008), Riverlark (N-009) and bonuses (N-010). Recommend a full mark-up holding playbook starting positions, with a note to Amelia Frost that no fallback has been exercised.
=== END ADVICE ===
